data.title: 13D Filings — Barrons.com
data.description:
These disclosures are from 13Ds filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. 13Ds are filed within 10 days of an entity's attaining more than 5% in any class of a company's securities. Subsequent changes in holdings or intentions must be reported in amended filings. This material is from Oct. 15 through Oct. 21, 2026. Source: VerityData

Activist Filings

Strata Critical Medical (SRTA) Third Point filed an initial 13D regarding its stake in the organ transport and medical logistics company, shifting to the stance of an activist investor from previous disclosures in a passive 13G. Third Point reported that it purchased 170,011 Strata Critical Medical shares from Aug. 31 through Oct. 13 at per share prices ranging from $4.53 to $5.66, after selling 43,500 shares from Aug. 31 through Sept. 30 at $5.11 to $5.66. Third Point said it believes the stock is undervalued and that Strata's business, while strong, isn't of a scale to support its current overhead, adding that management incentive options aren't aligned with creating shareholder value. The firm said Strata should explore strategic alternatives, including a potential sale managed by a reputable investment banking firm.

Following the latest activity, Third Point now owns 5,126,511 Strata Critical Medical shares, or 5.8% of those outstanding. Shares of Strata Critical Medical have lost roughly 4.7% of their value in 2026.

Increases in Holdings

Crescent Energy (CRGY)Independence Energy Aggregator raised its stake in the oil-and-gas producer to 68,655,357 shares. Independence Energy Aggregator did so through the purchase of 40,000,000 Crescent Energy shares on Oct. 8 at a price of $12.50 per share pursuant to an underwritten public offering.

Following the purchase, Independence Energy Aggregator owns a 16.3% stake in Crescent Energy's outstanding stock. Shares of Crescent Energy have gained approximately 57.6% in value in 2026.

Decreases in Holdings

Talos Energy (TALO) Carlos Slim lowered his stake in the oil-and-gas company to 24,500,000 shares. The Mexican billionaire reported that he sold 8,940,000 Talos Energy shares from Oct. 8 through Oct. 13 at per share prices ranging from $16.99 to $17.73.

Following the latest activity, Carlos Slim continues to own a 14.7% stake in Talos Energy's outstanding stock. Slim also disclosed a shift to passive investment intent in a 13G filing on Oct. 20 from previous disclosures in an active 13D. Shares of Talos Energy have gained roughly 59.7% in value in 2026.

Navigator Holdings (NVGS) BW Group lowered its stake in the liquefied-gas shipping company to 3,070,147 shares. BW Group did so through the sale of 988,931 Navigator Holdings shares from Oct. 2 through Oct. 15 at per share prices ranging from $22.00 to $24.66.

Following the latest sales, BW Group continues to own a 4.99% stake in Navigator Holdings' outstanding stock, placing BW Group below the 5% threshold that would require it to report further sales. Shares of Navigator Holdings have gained roughly 22.8% in value in 2026.

data.title: JetBlue creditors working with restructuring adviser PJT Partners, WSJ reports
data.description:
A senior creditors group to JetBlue Airways is working with restructuring adviser PJT Partners , the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

A surge in jet fuel expenses due to the Iran war has pressured margins for US airlines despite higher airfares and steady demand for air travel.

Here are some more details:

  • Shares of the carrier, which have fallen 42% this year, remained volatile in extended trading

  • JetBlue is also in the midst of a financial and operational overhaul to reduce costs, and plans to boost its premium offerings

  • As of June 30, JetBlue had $1.66 billion in cash and cash equivalents along with $8.5 billion of debt and finance lease obligations, according to its filings

  • JetBlue and PJT did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment

data.title: JetBlue Creditors Huddle With Restructuring Adviser as Bonds, Shares Sink — WSJ
data.description:
By Samantha Kroontje, Alexander Gladstone and Andrew Scurria

A group of senior creditors to JetBlue Airways is working with PJT Partners as the airline grapples with cash burn and elevated oil prices, according to people familiar with the matter.

JetBlue's bonds traded down sharply this week following a recent bondholder call. Its $2 billion notes due 2031 fell to 42 cents on Thursday before bouncing back slightly in the mid-40s on Friday, according to market participants and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, or Finra. They traded near 80 cents on the dollar earlier this month, Finra data shows.

A representative for JetBlue said the company is focused on strengthening revenue and building a more profitable business. The company plans to update its progress and financial outlook during its third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday.

PJT Partners declined to comment.

Write to Samantha Kroontje at samantha.kroontje@wsj.com, Alexander Gladstone at alexander.gladstone@wsj.com and Andrew Scurria at Andrew.Scurria@wsj.com

data.title: Basis flat, weekend rains may slow planting
data.description:
Basis bids for hard red winter wheat were unchanged at grain elevators in the southern US Plains on Friday, spot checks showed, while protein premiums rose for several wheat grades, typically a sign of demand from domestic flour mills.

  • Farmer sales were at a near standstill, one broker said, as K.C. hard red winter wheat futures fell for a seventh straight session, hitting three-month lows.

  • Growers remained focused on harvesting fall crops and seeding the winter wheat crop for harvest in mid-2027.

  • Rains were forecast for the southern Plains this weekend that were likely to slow fieldwork while also recharging soil moisture.

  • K.C. December hard red winter wheat futures (KWZ26) settled down 1-1/4 cents on Friday at $6.64-1/2 per bushel after dipping to $6.63, the contract's lowest since July 10.

  • Protein premiums for railcar wheat to and through Kansas City rose by 15 cents a bushel for wheat with 13.0% through 14.0% protein, while the premium for 11.6% protein fell by 6 cents.

data.title: S&P 500, Dow Drop As Elevated Oil Prices Stoke Inflation Fears Ahead Of Fed Meeting Next Week — AAPL, AXP, CART, UBER In Focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • The S&P 500 ended Friday 0.5% lower, the Nasdaq 100 was flat, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.2%.
  • The iShares Semiconductor ETF dropped for the third straight week.
  • Apple sold out its limited in-store inventory for the new iPhone Duo.

The S&P 500 and Dow Jones index ended lower on Friday as oil prices spiked amid resurfacing geopolitical concerns, which in turn raised inflation and rate hike worries ahead of the Federal Reserve’s October rate-setting meeting due next week.

The S&P 500 ended Friday 0.5% lower, the Nasdaq 100 was flat, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.2%. The Russell 2000, which tracks small-cap stocks, eased 0.3%.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) fell 0.5%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) fell 1.2%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) ended flat on Friday.

Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF slumped between 0.5% and 0.7% on Friday as gains in AMD, Micron Tech (MU) and Intel (INTC) offset weakness in Nvidia (NVDA). The broader Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT) rose 0.7%.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits for SPY, DIA and QQQ was ‘bearish’ with ‘high’ message volumes.

US Market Drivers

S&P 500-0.5%7,623.68
Nasdaq 100Flat28,957.53

A number of tech equities retreated as market participants weighed how surging corporate debt and elevated interest rates might impact AI-focused companies, particularly following Meta’s expanded capital expenditure forecast. Nevertheless, strong performances from SpaceX and Microsoft (MSFT) provided crucial support to the broader technology sector.

PhillipCapital completely reversed its bearish position, upgrading SpaceX shares from ‘sell’ to ‘buy,’ lauding the company’s advancements in AI or superintelligence.

“For the last two weeks, investors have been sprinting from tech stocks and data center beneficiary stocks to safe stuff, and eventually, you run out of people willing to do that sprint, and that’s what today looks like and feels like,” Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, told CNBC.

Meanwhile, West Texas Intermediate futures surged 3.8% to close at $103.27 per barrel. Similarly, Brent crude gained 3.1% to finish at $116.72 a barrel, marking its highest settlement since April amid reports the U.S. and Israel could be preparing fresh strikes against Iran. The United States Oil Fund (USO) ended its second week higher.

That spooked investors ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting due later next week. Market participants are currently betting on a 91% probability of the Fed leaving rates unchanged next week.

Key Trending Stocks

Instacart (CART) is actively exploring a potential sale, engaging financial advisers and holding preliminary discussions with prospective buyers, including rivals DoorDash (DASH) and Uber (UBER).

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed a lawsuit Friday against ChatGPT maker OpenAI and its chief executive, Sam Altman, alleging the organization engaged in deceptive trade practices, exposing consumers, including children.

American Express plans to eliminate about 5% of its global workforce.

Apple Inc. hit record highs on Friday after the firm quickly sold out of its limited in-store inventory for the new iPhone Duo.

Shares of Bloom Energy (BE) extended their post-earnings selloff in morning trade on Friday, but Morgan Stanley remained bullish on the fuel-cell maker’s growth prospects, citing growing confidence in its ability to ramp up production and convert customer demand into sales.

data.title: Hey, Bud. Don't Anger Your Customers — Barrons.com
data.description:
To the Editor: Sales of nonalcoholic beer aren't low because it doesn't taste like beer; they're low because it doesn't have any alcohol in it ("This Stock's for You: Buy Bud's 'Diet Coke' Moment," Cover Story, Oct. 14). I've been to Leuven, Belgium, many times. There are lots of bars, and the locals get it. Evidently, execs don't. If the thesis is that nonalcoholic beer is going to save Anheuser-Busch InBev, I'll fade it all day, every day. Here's another idea: Don't anger your customers with your marketing campaigns.

August West On Barrons.com

Tax Income, Not Assets

To the Editor: Taxation of the ultrarich is a difficult subject to agree upon, and probably always will be ("Taxes on the Wealthy Are on the Ballot in Many States. Could It Become a Federal Trend?" Oct. 15). But states need to be careful in how they go about it. If we tax the wealthy based on their assets, does that mean the government goes into their homes and assesses the value of their paintings, cars, and jewelry, or makes them open their safe-deposit boxes to determine the value of the items within? A tax where those with very large incomes pay their fair amount is easier to monitor than to try taxing wealth. We just need to agree upon the definition of a very large income and decide on a fair amount.

Thomas J. Kloepfer Buffalo Grove, Ill.

Dividend Discipline

To the Editor: John D. Rockefeller understood something that many investors have forgotten: Dividends are among the clearest expressions of shareholder ownership ("The S&P 500's Dividend Yield Is at an All-Time Low. What to Do If You're an Income Investor," Oct. 15). From a shareholder's perspective, a corporation is ultimately a machine for converting invested capital into sustainable cash distributions. While buybacks have their place, dividends represent a recurring financial commitment to shareholders. More importantly, dividend increases are among the loudest and clearest signals that management can send about its confidence in future earnings and cash flows. The S&P 500 index's historically low yield doesn't make dividends obsolete. It makes dividend discipline more important than ever.

Brad Thomas Greenville, S.C.

Labor Theory of Value

To the Editor:The propensity for a product or service to decrease in price is inversely proportional to the percentage of labor in said product or service ("Bond Investors See Inflation Cooling. Consumers See Anything But," The Economy, Oct. 16). In other words, because wages have a sticky upward bias, the higher the percentage of labor in a product or service, the less the price will come down when other comprising costs are reduced.

Steven R. Martin Northbrook, Ill.

data.title: GOAT Industries Signs Definitive Agreement To Acquire Epoxy AI Customer Contract Revenues
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada – October 23, 2026 - TheNewswire – GOAT Industries Ltd. (the “Company” or “GOAT”) (FWB: 26B.F) is pleased to announce, further to its

August 17, 2026 news release, that it and its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Source Gaming Company, operating as BetSource ("Source Gaming"), have entered into an arm’s length definitive contract revenue assignment agreement dated October 20, 2026 (the "Agreement") with Epoxy AI, LLC ("Epoxy") to acquire customer contract revenues from Epoxy (the "Transaction").

The Agreement represents a significant advancement of the Company's previously announced acquisition strategy, providing for the acquisition of all rights to revenues, receivables and other amounts payable under six Epoxy customer contracts with both US Tribal casinos, as well as other well known established casino and sports book operators, in exchange for 11,377,600 GOAT common shares at a deemed price of C$0.25 per share. The Company believes the six customer agreements represent a significant commercial opportunity relative to its existing operations.

Under the Agreement, Source Gaming will acquire the rights to revenues, receivables and other amounts payable under the six customer contracts (the "Contract Revenues") and Epoxy has agreed to assign the underlying customer contracts to Source Gaming within six months following closing, subject to obtaining any required customer consents. Until assignment, Epoxy will continue performing its contractual obligations under the six customer contracts and will hold revenues received under those contracts in trust for Source Gaming and remit them accordingly.

The Transaction supports GOAT's strategy to commercialize its BetSource technology platform across the U.S. Tribal gaming, commercial casino and sports betting markets. BetSource is designed to connect live sports, digital entertainment and personalized consumer experiences with new revenue opportunities, including advertising, sponsorships, customer acquisition and interactive gaming services.

"This Agreement marks an important step forward in delivering on the strategy we outlined to shareholders in August," said Hank Frecon, acting CEO of Source Gaming Company (BETSource) "The addition of these customer revenue streams represents a meaningful commercial opportunity for our business. By combining established customer relationships with our scalable BetSource technology platform, we believe we are building a foundation for continued growth across the gaming and sports entertainment industries."

Transaction Details

In consideration for the Contract Revenues, GOAT will issue Epoxy 11,377,600 common shares (the "Consideration Shares") at a deemed price of C$0.25 per share. The Consideration Shares will be issued in reliance on the asset acquisition prospectus exemption under National Instrument 45-106 – Prospectus Exemptions and may be subject to resale restrictions under applicable securities laws and escrow requirements under Canadian Securities Exchange ("CSE") policies.

Completion of the Transaction remains subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain conditions, including the release of all security interests in the Contract Revenues, receipt of necessary approvals and acceptance of the CSE. Either GOAT or Epoxy may terminate the Agreement if the Transaction is not completed by November 30, 2026. There can be no assurance that the Transaction will be completed on the terms described herein, or at all.

As previously disclosed, in connection with the parties' January 14, 2026 non-binding term sheet, GOAT advanced US$100,000 to Epoxy under a non-interest-bearing promissory note (the "Note"). The Note remains outstanding, will not be satisfied or extinguished as part of the Transaction, and will survive completion in accordance with its terms.

The securities referred to in this news release have not been, and will not be, registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "U.S. Securities Act"), or any state securities laws, and may not be offered or sold within the United States or to, or for the account or benefit of, U.S. persons (as defined in Regulation S under the U.S. Securities Act) unless registered under the U.S. Securities Act and applicable state securities laws or an exemption from such registration requirements is available.

GOAT Industries Ltd. is a digital media and technology company operating BetSource through its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Source Gaming Company. BetSource provides technology infrastructure designed to integrate live sports content, gaming applications, personalized consumer engagement and new digital monetization opportunities for media companies, casinos and sportsbooks.

data.title: The Plan to Put Super Dogs on the Battlefield of the Future — WSJ
data.description:
By Marcus Weisgerber and Heather Somerville

The U.S. military has long banked on new types of technology to give soldiers an edge on the battlefields of the future. A startup now wants dogs to have a similar advantage, genetically modifying man's best friend to make them run faster, have a keener sense of smell and avoid common genetic conditions.

The idea for a military super dog was conceived by Palmer Luckey, co-founder of defense tech firm Anduril Industries, and Ben Lamm, co-founder of Colossal Biosciences, a bioengineering company that aims to protect endangered species and bring back extinct animals.

Warhound said it has secured $200 million in its first funding round from investors, including In-Q-Tel, the CIA-linked venture-capital firm, and Sequoia Capital. Shaun Maguire, a partner at Sequoia who is leading the firm's investment, is a Pentagon adviser. The funding puts the company's valuation at $1.2 billion, according to PitchBook, a financial research firm.

Based in Texas, the company aims to collect cells from top-performing military and law enforcement dogs, then freeze them and clone the animals, Lamm said. It could then remove deleterious alleles — gene variants that can cause disease or defects — such as those associated with hip dysplasia or other genetic conditions. Eventually, the company aims to improve dogs' sense of smell, speed and agility.

Anduril, which makes weapons and software, will provide eye and hearing protection and body armor for the dogs. Colossal has an equity stake in Warhound, and Lamm sits on its board. Anduril has no stake in the company, and Luckey isn't a board member.

With nearly 90% of the military's working dogs purchased from overseas, Warhound also wants to increase the number of domestically sourced working dogs. "We have to do something to onshore what really is a living supply chain," said David Spirk, the company's chief executive.

The Air Force, which oversees military working dog training for the Pentagon, declined to comment on the new company. Luckey didn't respond to a request for comment.

Warhound said the dogs would be outfitted with the sensing technology. Anduril has developed an AI-powered helmet for humans that is supposed to give soldiers better awareness of their surroundings. The prototype is in early testing stages.

Warhound is starting its work with Belgian Malinois and German Shepherds, but plans to include Labradors and other breeds as well. Its first puppies are expected to be born in the first quarter of 2027.

Lamm began talking to Luckey about working dogs backstage at a conference about a year and a half ago.

Spirk, a former Marine who was the Pentagon's first chief data officer and previously worked at Palantir Technologies, said Warhound has 10 employees and is looking to hire military and law enforcement veterans with K9 experience.

The venture marks a new foray for Luckey, who has branched out from running Anduril, which was recently valued at $90 billion. His bank, Erebor Bank, received a national charter in February and is catering to startups and wealthy individuals.

Last month, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth chose Luckey to serve on a committee to study the future of warfare.

Colossal Biosciences has been on a quest to bring back extinct animals, including the woolly mammoth and dodo. The company has been panned by some academics and scientists, who doubt Colossal's claims of scientific breakthroughs and warn that introducing heavily genetically altered creatures can cause dangerous ecological disruption.

Lamm believes advances in AI, quantum computing and bioscience will allow the company to ultimately engineer new forms of life.

data.title: CME live cattle futures unchanged, feeder cattle futures firm
data.description:
Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures were mixed and feeder cattle ticked higher on Friday, as traders positioned ahead of the weekend and the US Department of Agriculture's cattle on feed report, released after the close of the trading session.

CME December live cattle ended the day unchanged at 231.125 cents per pound.

November feeders finished up 1.200 cents at 348.125 cents per pound.

Lack of fresh news and pre-weekend positioning resulted in lackluster trade on Friday, said Karl Setzer, co-founder of Consus Ag Consulting.

But after the session ended, the USDA released its monthly cattle on feed report, showing cattle on feed for slaughter as of October 1 at 100% of last year's numbers and just below the estimate of a Reuters poll of analysts that put them at 100.3% of the previous year.

Meanwhile September placements in feedlots were reported at 88% of last year's numbers, beneath the trade estimate of 92.6% and the lowest for September since 1996.

Wholesale boxed beef prices fell at midday on Friday to $365.79 per hundredweight (cwt) for choice cuts, down $3.68 from the previous day, while select cuts rose $2.29 to $352.69 per cwt.

Beef packer margins fell into the red at the end of the week. Packers lost an average of $4.10 per head, down from profits of $32.15 on Thursday, and $70.90 a week ago, according to livestock marketing advisory service HedgersEdge.

On Friday, 96,000 cattle were slaughtered, down from 102,000 a week ago, according to the USDA.

December lean hog futures (LHZ26) ticked up, ending 0.025 cent higher at 65.575 cents per pound.

The USDA reported prices for pork carcasses fell $1.14 to $74.09 per cwt, while bellies dropped $2.41 to $82.18 per cwt.

On Friday, 462,000 hogs were slaughtered, according to the agency, down from 472,000 a week ago.

data.title: Caldwell Announces Sale of IQTalent
data.description:
TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / October 23, 2026 / Caldwell , a leading retained executive search firm, today announced it has completed the sale of substantially all of the net operating assets of its wholly owned subsidiary, IQTalent Partners, Inc., to WinMil, Inc. WinMil will continue to operate the business under the IQTalent name and brand.

Caldwell acquired IQTalent in 2020 to broaden its service offerings into technology-enabled recruiting solutions at the professional level. After nearly six years, Caldwell determined that the business was not meeting the firm's strategic objectives and that a sale would better align its portfolio with its long-term priorities.

"Divesting IQTalent enables us to sharpen our focus on what Caldwell does best: delivering elite executive search and advisory services to our clients," said Chris Beck, chief executive officer of Caldwell. "IQTalent has been an important part of our portfolio, and we are proud of the innovative team and platform we helped build. We believe the business is well-positioned to succeed under WinMil's ownership, and we look forward to continuing a collaborative relationship through our referral partnership."

Founded in 2009, IQTalent pioneered an on-demand recruiting services model that blends proprietary technology with human expertise to deliver scalable talent acquisition solutions.

Transaction Terms

The transaction included the sale of substantially all of the net operating assets of IQTalent. Under the terms of the agreement, total consideration at closing was approximately $4.7 million, consisting of:

  • $3.2 million in cash, subject to exchange rate changes and a net working capital adjustment; and
  • 1.45 million Caldwell common shares held by David Windley and Tom Milic, who are owners of WinMil and former employees of IQTalent. The shares were valued at approximately $1.5 million, based on a simple average price of $1.05 per Caldwell share over the 20 days prior to closing. The shares have been cancelled by Caldwell, reducing total shares outstanding by approximately 4.9%.

All dollar amounts are presented in Canadian dollars.

Caldwell retains its minority equity interest in the recruitment software company HootRecruit (formerly known as IQRecruit). Caldwell also retains the ability to utilize IQTalent's remaining deferred tax assets to apply against future taxable ordinary income generated by Caldwell in the United States.

Caldwell and WinMil have also entered into a two-year referral agreement to connect clients with the firms' complementary executive search and recruiting services.

Caldwell's Board of Directors will evaluate the use of the cash proceeds as part of its capital allocation planning and expects to provide an update with the release of Caldwell's next quarterly earnings.

​​About Caldwell

Caldwell is an elite executive search firm trusted by established and growth-focused companies alike. For more than 50 years, we have partnered with clients to design and build extraordinary leadership teams. Our partners don't just place executives-they challenge assumptions, enable strategy, and prioritize long-term fit. Built on repeat clients and referrals, Caldwell delivers clarity and results without arrogance or shortcuts. Our suite of services includes executive and board level search, as well as talent strategy and assessment tools that help organizations hire the right people, then manage and inspire them to achieve maximum business results. For clients seeking substance over scale, we're the confident voice that listens-and leads. At Caldwell, our purpose is your mission.

Caldwell's common shares trade on The Toronto Stock Exchange and trade on the OTCQX Market . For more information, visit www.caldwell.com

data.title: Pepsi Tastes a Victory — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Evie Liu

PepsiCo has spent much of this year watching Coca-Cola poach its customers. This week, it had some better news: Yum! Brands' Taco Bell is staying put. The fast-food chain agreed Thursday to extend its beverage partnership with PepsiCo for another 11 years, keeping Pepsi, Mountain Dew, and other drinks flowing at participating U.S. restaurants through 2036.

The agreement follows a rough stretch in the cola wars. Last week, KFC said it would replace PepsiCo beverages with Coke at roughly 3,600 U.S. restaurants starting in January, ending a nearly 40-year relationship. Marriott made a similar switch in July after more than three decades with PepsiCo.

PepsiCo isn't retreating from the fight. The company is investing in technology and developing exclusive products to help its restaurant partners attract customers. For example, PepsiCo worked with Taco Bell to create Mountain Dew Baja Blast, now a billion-dollar brand, and Doritos Locos Tacos.

PepsiCo's sales to restaurants and other venues rose by a mid-single-digit percentage in the third quarter of 2025, and management reported further growth one year later. That's an encouraging sign as the company struggles with weak beverage demand in North America, where volumes fell 2% in the latest quarter.

The Taco Bell renewal isn't a new conquest. But after losing ground to Coca-Cola, defending a prized customer is a victory in itself.

Write to Evie Liu at evie.liu@barrons.com

Last Week

Whiplash

Wall Street was in love with tech again last week...and then fell out of love. The Nasdaq Composite, which was roughed up the week before, was up 2.2% through Wednesday, and then took a tumble.

Musklandia

Another crazy Elon week. Lawmakers want to know: Did Musk help Russia by restricting Ukraine's access to his Starlink network? Musk, who is also pushing a merger of his two companies, Tesla and SpaceX, is facing the possibility of a Democratic takeover of Congress — and a slew of subpoenas to follow. Is he worried? Well, he has so far sunk $366 million into this election cycle. So, yes.

Sahm's Take

The Fed meets Tuesday/Wednesday; the odds are slim it will vote to raise rates. But the New Century Advisors economic chief and super Substacker Claudia Sahm says board members should act now. Raising rates "reduces the odds" that "upside inflation risks...become reality and force larger hikes later." She adds: "A rate hike is not urgent, but is prudent."

Ticket scam?

In 2015, the Milwaukee Brewers sold "forever tickets" for $1,000. For what? Access to, well, an event like a World Series Brewers game. Hundreds cashed in, but were stuck with lousy seats. The Brewers then gave angry owners those seats and a ticket for a future game. By the way, if you had sunk $1,000 in the S&P 500 in 2015, it would be worth $4,000-plus now.

Next Week

Monday 10/26

This week is the busiest on the third-quarter earnings calendar, with about a?third of S&P 500 index companies slated to report results. Verizon Communications reports on Monday, followed by Boeing, Coca-Cola, and Visa on Tuesday. Alphabet, Ford Motor, GE Vernova, Microsoft, and?T-Mobile US release earnings on?Wednesday, while Amazon.com, Caterpillar, Eli Lilly, Intel, Mastercard, and Merck follow on Thursday. AbbVie, Chevron, and ExxonMobil Holdings report on Friday.

Wednesday 10/28

The Federal Open Market Committee announces its monetary-policy decision. The central bank is expected to keep the federal-funds rate unchanged at 3.75% to 4%, with traders pricing in only a 10% chance of a quarter-point interest-rate hike, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

Thursday 10/29

The Bureau of Economic Analysis releases the personal consumption expenditures price index for September. Economists forecast a 3.6% year-over-year increase, two-tenths of a percentage point more than in August. The core PCE price index is expected to rise 3.1%, compared with?3% previously.

The Numbers

Earnings-per-share growth at the S&P 500 companies reporting so far this earnings season.

Margin debt, its second-highest level on record, after soaring $26 billion in September.

NAHB/Wells Fargo index of home-builder confidence in October, off three points to lowest since 2012.

data.title: Brazil's central bank increases banks' disclosure obligations in offering credit
data.description:
Brazil's central bank announced on Friday a series of measures to strengthen the disclosure of financial institutions in offering and granting credit, in a move that comes amid growing concern among policymakers over household debt levels in the country.

The measures aim to provide consumers with more protection and information about credit offers, while reducing cases that may contribute to excessive indebtedness, it said in a statement.

  • The central bank will require banks to provide clients with mechanisms to block advertising and proactive credit offers

  • For financially vulnerable customers, "credit offers will require prior, specific and explicit authorization, and may only be aimed at improving their financial conditions," it said

  • Banks will have to provide customers with information on their existing credit operations, as well as simulations of the costs of new loans and alerts for higher-risk situations

  • The central bank also announced stricter rules governing credit offers during the initiation of transactions with the instant payment system Pix

  • The new measures will be effective between March and early July 2027

  • Reuters reported this week, citing sources, that the central bank was preparing a package of measures to curb rising household indebtedness, including stricter disclosure requirements for lenders
